title: Near Inclusions of von Neumann Algebras Without Small Spatial Embeddings
main_claim: There are separable Hilbert spaces H_n and von Neumann algebras M_n, N_n with gamma(M_n,N_n) -> 0. Spatial embeddings exist, but there is an eps_0>0 such that, for all large n, every unitary u with u M_n u* ⊆ N_n has ||u-I|| >= eps_0. This answers the unrestricted one-sided CCSSWW question in the negative.
coverage:
I checked the whole paper line by line.

Sec 2 (circle family):
- The tree vectors xi_x have norm one, and their Gram matrix is t^{d(x,y)}.
- The formula for T_g = pi(g)l(g)* holds: it is the identity off the path from e to g. On the path, T_g δ_{h_b} = r ξ_{h_b} − t δ_{h_{b+1}}, which I re-derived.
- Path entries are bounded by t^{|a-b|}.
- The twist D_z gives the identity pi_z(g) = (D_z T_g D_z*) l(g). Laurent exponents satisfy |k| <= |a-b|, so the row and column sums are <= 2t^{|k|}/(1-t). This gives S_0 and S_1 finite.
- The WOT limit pi_z(s_j) -> tz p_e holds: I recomputed pi_z(s_j)δ_e = tzδ_e + rδ_{s_j}.

Sec 3 (near-inclusion bound):
- The block formulas for Z and Y match the four-index expansions with D_{k,m}(X⊗I)D_{h,p}*.
- Y ∈ N because Y is invariant under right translation.
- The power-commutator bound |a||b|ν holds, so the reordering error is <= Σ c_k c_m c_p c_h |m-p||h| ν <= 2 S_0^2 S_1^2 ν.

Sec 4 (obstruction):
- The clock-shift commutator equals ω I, so κ = 1. The homotopy staying away from eigenvalue −1 is valid.
- Σ_n is a representation because u Z u* ∈ N commutes with ρ⊗I. The bound β_n = Cν_n + 2||u_n − I|| holds.
- The WOT limit of λρ on the conjugation slot is p_e. The tensor-slot WOT limits give t E_i R̃_i.
- WOT cluster points stay in A_in and inside the closed norm ball.
- Corner lemma: d <= δ(2+δ); the spectral projections Q_i lie in A_i; ||P − E|| is small; S E = P S and J E J* = P. The compressions P T_i P = A Q_2 and Q_1 B commute across adjoints. C_i is close to R_i because R̃_i commutes with E. The polar parts lie in commuting C*-algebras.
- The final subsequence/quantifier argument is correct.

The only external inputs are standard facts; the clock-shift obstruction is reproved in the paper.
sibling_notes: Family 289 had one sibling: rank 330, universal strong Kadison–Kastler stability, no_gap_found. It concerns two-sided perturbations, while this paper is explicitly one-sided and says it gives no counterexample to the two-sided Kadison–Kastler conjecture. The two papers share no lemmas, so there is no circularity.
